name: 3D printing / CAD
description: Parametric models in OpenSCAD: checked, exported, print-tested.
note: This is a 3D-modelling project in OpenSCAD (.scad files): models are code, built from named parameters, and exported to STL or 3MF for a slicer. Put every dimension in a parameter at the top (with a comment saying what it is and its unit, millimetres) and group them with /* [Group] */ comments for the Customizer; build shapes from small modules; set $fn high enough for smooth curves but not wastefully; leave 0.2 to 0.4 mm clearance between parts that must fit; keep walls at least 1.2 mm (two nozzle widths) and avoid overhangs steeper than 45 degrees or add the support in the model. Never guess a measurement of a real object: ask for it. After every change run the OpenSCAD check (errors, warnings, a valid solid) and, before exporting, Will it print for the user's bed size. OpenSCAD can read any file on the machine, so the tools compile only inside a sandbox: do not add include or import of paths outside the model's folder.
details: Designing parts as code. The 3D tool compiles an OpenSCAD model in a bubblewrap sandbox (no network, no home folder) and reports errors and warnings with their line and whether the result is a valid solid; exports STL, 3MF and a PNG picture; analyses any STL in plain arithmetic (triangles, size in millimetres, volume, surface area, watertight or not); checks whether a model will print on your bed (fit, watertight, thin parts, how much overhangs); lists the parameters a model is built from; and starts a parametric box.
